Subject: Post-call: migration mode recommendation & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and recommended next steps so we have alignment before the SE deep-dive: 

What we heard:
- Current setup: production calls to OpenAI API for most inference + a few large-batch jobs on legacy on-prem GPU clusters for heavy models.
- Volume: ~10k inference requests/day, peak bursts up to ~2k rps for short windows.
- Drivers: cost predictability (monthly spend), data residency/privacy (PHI in some flows), and performance consistency for low-latency features.
- Timeline: internal pilot targeted for Q4 2026; procurement / PO in parallel.

Preliminary recommendation (based on today's discussion):
1) Short-term: integrate via Redwood Hosted API for fastest time-to-value and to validate quality/latency with minimal infra work. This gets you live quickly and avoids lock-in while we run performance tests.
2) Medium-term: move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) once throughput patterns are stable to reduce unit cost and gain predictable latency. We can size the Dedicated cluster based on the pilot metrics.
3) Regulated/PHI flows: for anything requiring VPC/on-prem isolation, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem appliance). We can run a parallel private environment for those specific routes while keeping general traffic on Hosted/Dedicated.

Open items / asks (helps us prepare the SE session):
- Confirm approximate token volume per request (avg tokens in / out) and daily token volume target for pilot.
- Which endpoints need PHI isolation? A list of routes/features is fine.
- Any mandatory compliance docs (SOC 2, DPA, etc.)  we can share SOC2 summary and a short evidence checklist (attached).

Proposed next steps:
- SE technical deep-dive (60 min)  demo integration patterns + migration plan (we recommend Aug 20 or Aug 21). Marcus + David will lead.
- I’ll share: Dedicated pricing estimate, deployment-options one-pager, and SOC2 evidence request (attached).
- Fill the short questionnaire I’ll send (1 page) so we can size Dedicated and prepare the MAP / procurement docs.

Attachments: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf, soc2-evidence-request.pdf

Thanks  happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,

Thanks for the summary  a couple of technical notes we should cover in the SE session and the pilot plan:

1) Integration path:
- Phase 1 (Hosted): quick API key swap and traffic split (5-10% canary) to validate model parity. Use prefix caching for repeated prompts and short TTL to preserve freshness.
- Phase 2 (Dedicated): allocate reserved GPU pools based on pilot QPS and avg token sizes. We'll recommend quantization profile if cost is a main driver.
- Phase 3 (Private): run a VPC-connected control plane with customer-managed keys for PHI routes. We can map routes by header or different API key to keep traffic separated.

2) Migration best practices from other LLM APIs / self-hosted clusters:
- Start with mirrored read-only traffic to compare outputs (no user-facing changes).
- Use A/B gating with quiet canaries and smoke tests to detect regressions.
- For legacy GPU clusters, we typically recommend offloading high-throughput low-latency calls to Dedicated while keeping heavy batch jobs on existing infra during transition.

3) Performance tips for the pilot:
- Recommend batch sizes and target tokenization settings based on expected request mix (we'll size these after you share avg tokens).
- Plan for a 48-hour high-load soak test to validate autoscaling and KV cache hit rates.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and share the internal SE playbook link prior to the demo: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-example-se-playbook

-David
